raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with smooth, lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads), a classic radiographic sign of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma or other lymphoproliferative disorders in this location. The absence of vertebral destruction makes metastatic disease less likely, and the smooth margins argue against an abscess or irregular metastases.
